xep.header:
HTTP File Upload Deletion This specification defines a protocol to delete files uploaded via HTTP File Upload (XEP-0363). &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council
XMPP Core XEP-0001 XEP-0030 XEP-0363
http-upload-delete
Linus Jahn lnj@kaidan.im lnj@kaidan.im
0.0.1 2022-10-14 lnj
First draft.

section1.p: &xep0363; defines a way to upload arbitrary files. It does not forbid servers to delete uploaded file, however, it does not define a way to delete files. There are different reasons why a user might want to do that:

ul.li: To avoid further distribution of an accidentially shared file. It should not happen, but it still does.
To free up space for new files in case the storage is limited. This avoids that the server automatically deletes a file (e.g. the oldest) when uploading new files.
To delete undesirable or reported files, as an administrator.
Provide a simple IQ request to delete a file.
Do not require more information than the HTTP GET URL of the file.

section2.p: An HTTP File Upload service advertises support for file deletion by providing the urn:xmpp:http:upload:delete:0 feature in its &xep0030; features.
section2.example: <iq from='upload.montague.tld' id='disco' to='romeo@montague.tld/garden' type='result'> <query xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info'> <identity category='store' type='file' name='HTTP File Upload'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:http:upload:0'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:http:upload:delete:0'/> <x type='result' xmlns='jabber:x:data'> <field var='FORM_TYPE' type='hidden'> <value>urn:xmpp:http:upload:0</value> </field> <field var='max-file-size'> <value>5242880</value> </field> </x> </query> </iq>

section2.p: A client may delete a file by sending a <delete/> request to the HTTP File Upload service handling the URL. The IQ request MUST be of type 'set' and MUST have a <delete/> element from the urn:xmpp:http:upload:delete:0 namespace. It MUST have an 'url' attribute with the GET URL of the file to be deleted.

example.caption: User requests deletion of a file

section2.p: The service needs to identity the file. It SHOULD only accept URLs of the same form as it generates. It MUST NOT open HTTP requests or try to follow redirects to indicate the file.

The service MUST check that the XMPP entity is allowed to delete the file. The service SHOULD NOT allow regular users to delete files of other users. It SHOULD allow users to delete files uploaded by the same bare JID.

section3.p: If the service was able to identify the file based on the URL, could verify the requesting entity is allowed to delete the file by the service policy and the file has been deleted permanently, it MUST return an empty IQ result.

example.caption: Service indicates that the file has been deleted

section3.p: The service MUST return an error for HTTP requests on the URL. The HTTP error MAY indicate that this file has been deleted manually.
In case the URL is well formed, the domain is handled by this service, but the file does not exist, the service SHOULD return an IQ of type 'error' with

section3.topic: User is not allowed to delete the file

section3.p: In case the provided URL is no valid HTTP URL or the domain from the URL is not handled by the service.
